# AJ Wiebe

> Personal website of AJ Wiebe, software engineer and principal consultant at Bitovi. Covers ontologies, knowledge graphs, AI agents, and what AJ is building now.

## Pages

- [Home](https://systemsbyaj.com/): Introduction, recent writing and projects
- [About](https://systemsbyaj.com/about.html): Bio, from research to software development to technical leadership
- [Résumé](https://systemsbyaj.com/resume.html): Public career summary and education
- [Research](https://systemsbyaj.com/research.html): Published papers, master's thesis, current research topics
- [Projects](https://systemsbyaj.com/projects/): What AJ builds and why
- [Writing](https://systemsbyaj.com/writing/): Articles (none published yet)

## WebMCP tools

Every page registers WebMCP tools (document.modelContext) in browsers that support it. They return the site's content as structured JSON and are read-only, except set_theme.

- about_this_website: what the site is, every page, the latest posts, the other tools
- about_aj_wiebe: bio, work history, education, projects, research and contact links in one call
- get_current_page: the content of the page that is open, as structured sections
- list_pages, get_page: every page, and any page's content as structured sections
- list_projects, get_project: the projects and their full write-ups
- get_experience: résumé and education
- list_research: publications and research interests
- list_posts, get_post: the blog posts, and one post's structured data (thesis, audience, claims with evidence types, limitations, sources, disclosures, next steps)
- search_site: full-text search across all pages and posts
- set_theme: switch between light and dark themes

Blog post pages (under /writing/) also register tools about the post that is open:

- get_post_summary: thesis, takeaways, outline
- check_post_fit: who the post is for and not for, prerequisites, limitations
- get_post_credibility: author's experience with the topic, dates, versions tested, known outdated parts, disclosures
- get_post_claims: each claim with its evidence type (measured, experienced, cited, opinion) and link
- get_post_context: sources it builds on, supports or contradicts, related posts
- get_post_next_steps: what to do next, and when not to

The same tools can be called from page JavaScript in any browser, including ones without WebMCP:

- window.siteTools.list(): tool names, descriptions and input schemas
- await window.siteTools.call("about_this_website", {}): returns the same JSON string as the WebMCP tool
- window.siteTools.webmcp: which API registered the tools (document.modelContext or navigator.modelContext), or null
- The data-webmcp attribute on <html> shows the status: registered, partial, failed or unavailable

The full page and post index is at https://systemsbyaj.com/webmcp-index.json. The site-wide and post tools
come from the quarto-webmcp extension: https://github.com/alexanderwiebe/quarto-webmcp
